Commentary.Commentary: That is it from us today. West Indies have fought back with a bang to keep the series alive. India lacked intent with the bat today. That is the reason they lost a game which they should have won. There is a lot to play for in the final match of the ODI series. It will take place on 6th July in Kingston at 0900 local time (1400 GMT). Do join us for all the action. Till then, goodbye and cheers!

West Indies skipper and Man of the Match, Jason Holder says that he is extremely pleased with his performance. Credits all the other bowlers as well. Adds that they were terrific in the field today. Mentions that India's top order has been doing very well in the past. Also says that getting Dhawan and Kohli early on helped them take hold of things. States that he is proud of Kesrick Williams and praises him for the maturity he showed in his second match. Opines that batting is definitely an area of concern and they will look to rectify it. Reckons that he needs to stick to a plan and bowl consistent lines and lengths. Ends by saying that they need to keep believing in themselves and give their best.

India skipper, Virat Kohli says that they bowled well but admits they were not up to the mark with the bat. Opines small totals are tricky at times. Credits the West Indian bowlers for bowling in the right areas and building pressure on the Indian batsmen. Informs the pitch was a little two-paced. Further adds it was okay with the new ball but batting got difficult later on. Feels the bowling and fielding were on point but the batting faltered. Ends by saying they have to come out stronger in the next game.

The skipper was the star of the show and this was his best figures in ODIs. All the other bowlers were tidy and didn't let the Men in Blue run away. Especially the spinners, Bishoo and Nurse were right on the money and made life difficult for the middle order. The opposition batsmen were also guilty of poor shot selections. Defending 189 is not an easy job but credit to them for bowling exceedingly well and snatching victory from the jaws of defeat.

Jason Holder was sharp with his captaincy and set attacking fields. There weren't easy singles on offer and the visitors failed to rotate strike on a consistent basis. There was a 54-run stand between Dhoni and Rahane but it came off 109 balls. Both of them scored half centuries but it can be said they were pretty slow. With Dhoni still at the crease in the 49th over, the tourists believed in themselves. However, his downfall almost decided the fate of the game. Holder held his nerves and bowled a tight final over to take his side over the finishing line.

What a game of cricket! Kudos to West Indies for battling it out till the end and emerging victorious. With the batting line-up India possesses, it seemed at the halfway stage that it will be a cakewalk in the park for them but the home side had other ideas. They used the two-paced nature of the track to great effect and choked the Indian batsmen. The early departure of Dhawan and Kohli allowed the hosts to apply more pressure.

WEST INDIES WIN BY 11 RUNS.
Yorker on off, Kuldeep digs it out towards short fine leg for a single. He has a shy at the striker's end but misses.

Fires it on the stumps, Pandya drives it past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a run.

Length ball on off, Dhoni defends it off the front foot.

Wide outside off, Dhoni lets it through to the keeper.

Full on off, Dhoni drives it to covers.

West Indies would want to build on this wicket now. Can they put more pressure on India?

Full length ball outside off, stroked exquisitely to short extra cover for no runs.
Fuller length ball, Rahane eases it to covers.
Shortish delivery around off, not much room to work with. Ajinkya stays back and chops it to point.

Fractionally overpitched outside off, Rahane times it beautifully towards mid off. Holder dives to his right and saves a certain boundary for his side. His teammate comes around and pats him on his back. The skipper looks to be in a bit of pain, he is holding his knee.
In the channel outside off, third leave in a row.
Dug in short around off, Karthik arches back and lets it go.
Good length delivery but it is well outside off, Dinesh covers his stumps and leaves it alone.
Fullish delivery and tailing into Rahane. He goes for the flick but gets it off the inner half to fine leg. A run taken.
Another full length ball and Rahane drives it crisply but it is straight to mid off.
Fullish ball on off, eased to mid off.
Back of a length around off, Karthik is indecisive with his footwork as he gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Dropped! You can't get an easier catch than that and unfortunately, Mohammed has spilled it. Fullish delivery and angling into the pads, Rahane clips it but doesn't bother keeping it down. It flies straight towards Jason who puts down a dolly. Single taken.
FOUR! Comical stuff! Full length delivery, Rahane strokes it towards mid off. The tall Jason Holder bends to stop it but it goes right through his legs and to the fence. That was sloppy.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, Rahane doesn't bother to play at it.
Length ball well outside off, driven through cover-point for a brace.
Dinesh Karthik comes out to bat.

OUT! Holder outsmarts his opposite number! Brilliant thinking from the West Indies skipper and he gets the reward. Holder hits the deck hard and bowls it outside off, Kohli once again shuffles a touch and looks to pull it over mid-wicket. However, he gets deceived by the extra bounce and that brings the top edge. The ball skies just behind the stumps. Shai Hope runs forward and pouches it safely. Crucial breakthrough for West Indies.
Length delivery, shaping in. Kohli pushes it down the track.
Short of a length outside off, Kohli looks to defend it off his back foot but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Beaten! Kohli transfers his weight on the front foot and Holder bangs in a bouncer in his line. He goes for the hook but misses it completely. This is going to be an interesting contest.
Good length delivery around off, Kohli shuffles across and taps it with soft hands to mid on.
In the channel outside off, Virat doesn't fiddle with it.
Stays back to the good length delivery and taps it square of the wicket on the off side. 11 from the over, good one for India.
That surprised Ajinkya! Back of a length on off, zips through the pitch. The right-hander hops back and fends it off towards point.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Gets another short delivery and he was waiting on the back foot for it. Pulls it with authority over backward square leg to find the fence.
FOUR! That is a shot of a man in form. Joseph bangs it in short and Rahane takes him on. Nails the pull over square leg to pick up a one-bounce boundary.
Length delivery outside off, punched on the up to mid off.
Pure timing! Fullish delivery outside off, Kohli shuffles across and times it beautifully through mid-wicket. Gets three runs to his name.
Short delivery outside off, sits up nicely for Rahane. He goes for the pull but misses.
Fuller length ball on off, pushed to mid off from the front foot.

Loud shout for an LBW denied! Holder steams in and bowls a good length delivery on middle and off. Gets it to shape in as Rahane misses his flick to get rapped on the pads. Confident shout from the home side but the umpire stays put. Holder looks at Shai Hope who indicates that it would have gone down leg. So, no review taken. The replays also show it was sliding down.
Good length delivery on off, defended solidly off the back foot.
FOUR! Shot! Back of a length outside off and room on offer, Rahane rises on his toes and slaps it over extra cover. The fielder hares after it but comes second best.
Full length ball on middle, Rahane eases it to mid on.
Kohli moves across to the length delivery and clips it to the leg side. Successful over for West Indies. Joseph bags a wicket maiden to his name.
Short of a length and angling into Kohli. He tucks it to square leg.
Wide outside off, Virat lets it through.
Back of a length on off, Kohli tucks it nicely to mid-wicket.
Full length ball outside off, Kohli puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Virat Kohli comes out to bat.

OUT! Soft dismissal! On a length and on the pads, Dhawan looks to clip it through but ends up chipping it straight towards Holder at short mid on who accepts the easiest of catches with glee. Perhaps, the sticky nature of the track did him in. Credit to Holder as well for his field placement. Usually mid on is deeper but it was positioned well this time. West Indies strike early but they need to keep getting wickets regularly.
In the channel outside off, Rahane points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Short delivery outside off, cut hard past point for a run.

Back of a length ball on off, Rahane hops back to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards point and Dhawan is aware of the situation. Calls his partner through and completes the run with ease

Well played! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Dhawan drives it elegantly through covers. The outfield is not that quick and the ball rolls towards the fence. Two fielders chase it down. Keep it down to three.
Shortish outside off, not much room this time. Shikhar looks to cut it but ends up chopping it to point.

Wide! Holder comes around the wicket and angles in a back of a length delivery towards the rib cage of Dhawan. He moves inside the line and looks to tuck it around the corner but misses. The ball sails into the gloves of the keeper and the players appeal. However, the umpire signals it as a wide. Replays show that there was no bat involved.
Fuller length ball well outside off, Dhawan plants his front foot across and allows it through.
Jason Holder to bowl with the second new ball.
Dug in short but the line is wrong. It is down the leg side and it is helped on its way to fine leg for a run. He is off the mark as well.
Good length ball on off, pushed off the back foot to point.

In the air... but safe! Joseph bowls a well-directed bouncer on off and gets it to climb on Rahane. He fails to control the pull and it goes off the top edge towards fine leg. Roston Chase runs in but the ball falls short of him. That was nicely bowled.
On a good length and angling into Rahane. He hops and tucks it past the diving square leg fielder. Two runs taken.
Fullish delivery outside off, Rahane strokes it sweetly towards mid off. Holder runs to his right and slides to save some runs for his side.
Short of a length and width on offer, Rahane places it to backward point where Kyle Hope dives to his right to make a good stop.

We are back for the chase. Shikhar Dhawan and Ajinkya Rahane will open the batting for India. The West Indies team is in a huddle. They will need some quick wickets to put pressure on the Men in Blue. Alzarri Joseph to start off the proceedings with the ball. A slip in place. Here we go...
